kept.excerpt: Sulyok said he had no reason to resign and that the prime minister had not found a public-law justification for removing him. He argued that the proposed seventeenth constitutional amendment targeted the incumbent president personally and was incompatible with the rule of law.
kept.relevance: Documents Sulyok's continued resistance immediately before the evidence cutoff, making voluntary resignation distinct from the government's proposed removal route.

kept.excerpt: Following public consultation, the government submitted its proposed seventeenth amendment to the Fundamental Law to Parliament on Saturday. Magyar said Sulyok would certainly no longer be president around July 20. Under the proposal, Parliament would elect a replacement for a period ending when a new constitution entered into force, subject to a maximum of five years.
kept.relevance: Establishes that a concrete removal proposal had been submitted and records the prime minister's stated timetable within the market's July deadline.

kept.excerpt: President Sulyok met Venice Commission President Marta Cartabia, Director and Secretary Simona Granata-Menghini, and Austrian member Christoph Grabenwarter at the Sándor Palace. He had requested the commission's assistance on May 29 to resolve the constitutional conflict following the elections. The commission indicated its readiness to consider the submission urgently and obtain information through consultations in Budapest.
kept.publisher: Sándor Palace — Office of the President of Hungary
kept.relevance: Provides official evidence that Sulyok was still exercising presidential functions and pursuing an international constitutional response to the dispute.

kept.excerpt: The Hungarian Helsinki Committee submitted its opinion on the draft seventeenth amendment, objecting to the five-day consultation period and insufficient justification for proposed changes. It considered Sulyok's removal potentially justified by the need to restore the rule of law, but said the government must explain the underlying arguments in detail in the amendment's explanatory memorandum.
kept.relevance: Supplies a primary legal assessment supporting the possibility of removal while identifying procedural and justification issues that could complicate implementation.

kept.excerpt: Two Hungarian rights groups criticised a draft constitutional amendment proposing President Tamas Sulyok's removal and a term limit for members of Parliament. Amnesty International Hungary considered Sulyok unworthy of office but objected to the government's chosen removal procedure. Political analyst Gabor Torok also criticised removing the head of state through a one-sentence constitutional amendment.
kept.relevance: Shows that objections to the removal mechanism extended beyond the political opposition and could create pressure for procedural changes or delay.

kept.excerpt: Magyar told Parliament that the government would initiate the termination of Sulyok's presidential mandate. He said Parliament would elect a replacement until completion of the constitution-making process, for no more than five years.
kept.relevance: Records the government's publicly stated legislative objective and replacement plan before formal submission of the amendment.

kept.excerpt: Hungary's government said it would amend the constitution to remove President Tamás Sulyok after the May 31 resignation deadline. Magyar's Tisza party held a two-thirds parliamentary majority, enabling constitutional changes. The president could refer legislation to the Constitutional Court for review.
kept.relevance: Establishes the government's constitutional voting capacity and the institutional conflict underlying the effort to remove Sulyok.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-06, inclusive. All included items have publication dates verified in web_search results or dated source text exposed by search. Hungarian excerpts are factual English translations or close paraphrases, not verbatim English quotations. Later-dated material, undated pages, prediction markets, betting pages, odds, and market prices were excluded. The July 20 timing is a contemporaneous statement attributed to Magyar, not an independently established effective date. Full-page verification was limited: web_fetch failed because multiple providers were registered, and the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED; no further fallback reads were attempted after that response. The pack therefore relies on search-indexed source evidence and does not claim successful full-page retrieval.
